messages:
frank: Heads-up: noticed a small rise in cross-region hedging and surprising cost churn after the latest policy roll. The pattern looks different from epoch drift — it's more about compatibility checks being expensive and some routers falling back to conservative cost-heavy variants.
alyssa: dug into traces. routers are doing a compatibility full-graph eval when they see a new snapshot fingerprint. That eval is CPU-heavy and sometimes times out -> fallback to safe (expensive) model variants.
kevin_m: interesting. two orthogonal fixes: 1) make compatibility checks cheap/approximate at runtime (fast path) and 2) decouple compatibility from heavy semantic checks by publishing richer compatibility metadata from the compiler.
sophie: idea: publish a compact compatibility bloom + small vector of capability bits per snapshot. Routers can do a quick bloom membership test to accept/decline candidates. If bloom says "possibly compatible" then schedule a deferred deep-check async, otherwise immediate reject and use fallback. Bloom keeps runtime cheap and avoids CPU timeout fallback.
frank: +1. bloom false-positive rate is acceptable because deep-check runs afterwards and can signal a corrective route if needed. We should pick bloom params so fp rate < 0.5% for snapshots in last 30d.
alyssa: also propose adding per-tenant cost-sensitivity metadata. Some tenants are cost-sensitive and would rather accept slightly higher latency; others want lowest latency at any cost. Publish tenant.routing_profile = ["cost_aware", "latency_aware", "balanced"]. Router scoring uses this to prefer candidate variants. Combine with bloom so we avoid picking expensive variants just because deep-compatibility timed out.
kevin_m: tradeoffs: bloom + profile reduces CPU but adds a new surface. Need to think about snapshot churn: many small snapshots could bloat bloom sets. Solution: epoch-windowed bloom + TTL eviction and compact delta publishing.
sophie: runtime sketch:
```
- on snapshot publish: policy-service emits {snapshot_id, compact_compat_bloom, capability_bits, seed_version}
- router fast-path: candidate filtering = candidate.fingerprint in bloom && (capability_bits & tenant.needs) == tenant.needs
- if fast-path passes -> route candidate; concurrently schedule deep-compatibility-check (async)
- if deep-check rejects -> emit routing.corrective_decision and optionally retry request if within request TTL
- if fast-path fails -> use fallback policy (per-tenant allow|prefer|strict)
```
frank: what about immediate customer-visible regressions if deep-check later rejects? We shouldn't silently change the returned answer. Maybe corrective decision only used for subsequent requests unless request context allows buffered retry.
alyssa: Agreed. For now corrective only affects subsequent requests. We can add cooperative retries in a future pass where the client accepts idempotent replay.
kevin_m: instrumentation: routing.compat_bloom_fp_rate, routing.fastpath_accept_rate, routing.deepcheck_reject_rate, routing.cost_variant_selection_rate_by_tenant_profile. Also track hedges vs bloom-accepts.
sophie: rollout plan: 1) compiler: emit compact_compat_bloom (configurable K bits) + capability bits (sophie) 2) router: implement fast-path bloom test + async deep-check (alyssa) 3) simulate with recorded traffic (frank) 4) staging prefer-mode with bloom enabled 5) 1% canary strict in production.
ops-bot: "policy-compiler: compat-bloom feature flag enabled in staging at 2026-06-08T08:12:00Z"
frank: extra safety: seed the bloom only for snapshots that are semantically small deltas. For large changes mark snapshot as "large-change" and force strict deep-check until warmed. Also add a safety throttle so no more than X snapshots per minute are bloom-published to avoid thrash.
alyssa: small note on sizing: choose bloom per-tenant-shard with target entries = recent_snapshot_count_per_shard and bits = entries * 10 to hit <0.5% fp. We'll add a quick calcer in the compiler that outputs suggested parameters.
kevin_m: I'll add dashboard tiles and an alert if routing.fastpath_accept_rate drops below baseline or if deepcheck_reject_rate > 0.2%. Also add a regression alert if hedges rise >1.0% post-roll.
sophie: final ask: add explainability fields to the response metadata: {used_fastpath: true|false, bloom_snapshot_hint: id, capability_bits_matched: []}. Helps debugging and customer support.
frank: thanks. I'll open the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and bloom param experiments. Please add sim configs to the PR. Ping me if you want to pair. :thumbsup:
